description: A four-person team is working on a project themed "Abandoned but not Forgotten"—an exploration of NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars, presented through a map and dynamic, interactive narratives. Prior experience is not the primary requirement; what matters most is the drive to see the prototype through to completion and the ability to work effectively as a team. Languages: Russian and English. Format: in-person.
summary: Almost everyone knows Apollo 11, but few people know that dozens of landers, rovers and crashed probes still lie on the Moon and Mars, and their stories are scattered across technical tables. We built "Abandoned but not Forgotten", a free online museum that places 26 of these objects on real NASA maps of the Moon and Mars. Each object has a story card (what it did, why it stayed, what it gave to science), coordinates with an accuracy label and a link to its source. Pupils can explore a 3D globe, compare mission-era photos with orbital images, take a quiz, or use an AR table with a printed map. It opens in any browser with no sign-up. This is a great opportunity for NASA to integrate our project into its educational platforms for students.
details:
WHAT IT DOES
"Abandoned but not Forgotten" is an interactive online museum about the hardware humans left on the Moon and Mars. It features a 2D map and a 3D globe, a mission timeline, a NASA photo archive, Before/After views (a photo from the mission era next to an orbital image from LRO or HiRISE), the "Forgotten Relics" exhibition (15 relics, 5 stories), a 54-question quiz, and an AR table that works with printed markers and a smartphone.

HOW IT TELLS THE STORIES
Every object has a card detailing what it did, why it was left behind, and what it contributed to science. A "Mission Journey" tracks each mission from launch to legacy.

REAL DATA, HONESTLY LABELLED
Maps use NASA Moon Trek and Mars Trek tiles. Photos are searched live in the NASA Image and Video Library and kept only when NASA's own metadata names the same mission or object. Each coordinate has an accuracy label (measured, approximate, or area) and every record links to its source. Equipment condition is assigned manually with a reason and a source; unknown stays "Unknown". 3D models and illustrations are schematic and labelled as such.

INTERACTIVE AR EXPERIENCE

The platform integrates a printable AR-marker system, available on the website under the "Markers to print" section. Using the first sheet, "AR table markers," users define a map area on any flat surface, projecting an interactive model of the Moon or Mars directly through a smartphone camera. The second sheet, "Robot marker," attaches to a physical moving object, such as an RC car. By driving the car across the mapped zone, students control a virtual rover to navigate to and explore authentic NASA landing sites and retired spacecraft. This hands-on approach turns planetary science and space history into an engaging classroom experiment.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

NASA can use this project as an effective tool to promote space exploration and engage K-12 and college students in STEM at an early stage of their education. The platform is free, requires no account or installation, and opens via a simple link on a computer or phone, making it ready for immediate classroom use. Students learn the history of Moon and Mars exploration and see how real space data is applied. With new landers heading back to the Moon, mapping and protecting these heritage sites matters now more than ever.

TOOLS

HTML, CSS, and JavaScript (static site, no build step), a custom WebGL 2 globe engine, AR marker detection in plain JavaScript, Leaflet 1.9.4 for the 2D map, a PWA service worker, and Python scripts for data checks and screenshots. A dedicated promo page is also included.

SOURCE CODE (Apache License 2.0)

https://github.com/CARTEZteam/CARTEZteam.github.io

NEXT STEPS

Extend the catalogue to all landers, rovers, and impact sites; publish it as an open dataset; display planned landing zones alongside heritage sites; and bring the virtual museum and AR table to schools and science centres.
